designDecisions.decision: Used the value only to justify a bespoke estate-scale composition with a dominant living pavilion, suite pavilions and resolved outdoor sequence.
designDecisions.limitation: No valuation, cost estimate or luxury certification is claimed.

designDecisions.decision: Placed arrival and private suite entries on one side of the composition and directed terrace and pool sequence toward the assumed water view.
designDecisions.limitation: No surveyed shore, flood datum, setback or marine work is modeled.

designDecisions.decision: Constructed a rectangular basin with floor, perimeter walls, coping and dry decks at the end of the terrace sequence.
designDecisions.limitation: Overflow hydraulics and a true engineered infinity edge are unsupported.

designDecisions.decision: Used deep roof eaves, shaded terrace canopy and selective view glazing for a climate-responsive exterior.
designDecisions.limitation: Wind, corrosion, thermal and hurricane performance are not verified.

designDecisions.decision: Organized a legible sequence of drive, arrival, shared living, shade and pool, with private pavilions subordinate to the central volume.
Replaced the central rear wall with a fitted, real garden-door bay facing the terrace and pool.
designDecisions.limitation: The adjacent glazing is limited to the constructed bay; no glare or view simulation is provided.

designDecisions.decision: Considered a mono-pitch ventilated roof; selected coordinated hip and gable roofs instead to distinguish the central pavilion from quieter suite pavilions.
designDecisions.limitation: Ventilated ridge, gutters and rainwater systems are not constructed.

designDecisions.decision: Applied the principle of a clear vehicle approach terminating at a protected pedestrian threshold.
designDecisions.limitation: No gate, turning analysis, lighting or planted median is constructed.

limitations: Surface areas are per physical element; overlapping surfaces are not additional usable area. Enclosed area, requested-space completeness, pool construction and circulation require architectural review. A renderable model is not a completed building.
